A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PRISM research. All 23 pages of v2 and 24 pages of v3, including appendices, equations, tables and figures, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original Sudoku, OpenWebText and MBPP experiments, including hyperparameter ablations in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds HumanEval evaluation and an OpenWebText per-token score analysis.

M1.justification: The PRISM loss, shared backbone and quality head, regularization, LoRA option and inference procedures remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–4 match across versions.

E1.justification: HumanEval adds another Python coding benchmark alongside MBPP. Sudoku, OpenWebText and the coding fine-tuning dataset are retained; coverage expands within an existing domain.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparator sets. HumanEval extends evaluation of the existing MDM, ReMDM and ReMDM-conf baselines; the removed related-work citations were not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The new diagnostic uses 256-step generation without remasking and documents score binning and likelihood queries after masking the evaluated token. Existing training and coding settings are retained; no protocol revision explains the changed MBPP scores.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendix D.5 add an analysis intended to assess posterior calibration across generation stages, displayed in Figure 7. The existing Sudoku visualization and token-count and nucleus-sampling ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new score-distribution diagnostic does not introduce uncertainty estimates for experimental results.

E6.justification: v3 adds a complete HumanEval comparison and Figure 7's score-distribution results, while revising every MBPP entry. At 256/512/1024 steps, PRISM's MBPP scores change from 23.0/30.5/32.9% in v2 Table 1 to 21.8/29.1/32.3% in v3 Table 2. Its 1024-step ranking against ReMDM-conf reverses. New HumanEval scores are 28.0/39.0/42.7%. Sudoku, OpenWebText benchmark scores and existing ablation results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The masking-process equivalence, Propositions 1–2 and their derivations and proofs are retained. Appendix B gains an empty subsection heading and renumbering, without new mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement and conclusion retain the claims of lightweight, theoretically grounded self-correction across domains and model scales. HumanEval supplies additional evidence for the existing coding claim.

C2.justification: v3 newly interprets score agreement as evidence of well-calibrated target-posterior estimation. The reference is a pretrained-model likelihood, and Figure 7 displays overlaid score histograms rather than the described bin-wise calibration curves. Existing diversity and global-reasoning limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 Table 3 newly identifies dagger-marked MDLM and ReMDM results as taken from Wang et al. (2025); v2 Table 2 lacked that attribution. This disclosure leaves tension with the retained statement that baselines were reevaluated after fine-tuning. Hardware, adapters and hyperparameter information otherwise match.

R1.justification: v3 removes the concurrent-work discussion and references to Meshchaninov, Li and Huang et al. (2025), including Appendix A's explicit comparison with Huang's similar training pipeline. It adds Chen (2021) for HumanEval. The broader related-work taxonomy remains intact.

P1.justification: Changes are localized to the removed concurrent-work passages, added quantitative-analysis paragraph and appendix subsection, revised coding-results prose and subsection renumbering. Most wording and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figure 7 and places separate HumanEval and MBPP tables side by side. Figure 4 gains a clearer caption, and the OpenWebText table gains attribution markers. Existing figure artwork is unchanged, with limited relocation and page reflow.

improvement.justification: HumanEval broadens empirical validation, and baseline attribution adds transparency. These gains coexist with removal of the comparison to Huang et al. (2025), which v2 identifies as most relevant, and unexplained MBPP score revisions. Figure 7 also shows histograms rather than the calibration curves described in its caption, limiting the new mechanistic evidence. These tradeoffs prevent a reliable judgment of net quality improvement.
